surface_mechanism_description: The nitrogen atoms in the interfacial region of the HfO2 films effectively blocked oxygen diffusion during subsequent annealing in a N2 atmosphere. The nitrogen atoms incorporated in the HfO2 films during deposition were thought to be useful in preventing the growth of the interfacial layer between the HfO2 and Si after annealing. The high reactivity of the N2O plasma efficiently decomposed the diethyl-amine group in the plasma process.
